summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of kidney and pancreas transplants was admitted with fever, rigors, and right leg cellulitis. She had recently been treated for acute cellular rejection of her pancreas transplant and was on immunosuppressive therapy. Blood cultures identified E. coli bacteremia, and she was started on intravenous antibiotics and fluids for sepsis. Her condition improved with treatment, and a PICC line was placed to complete a 14-day course of IV vancomycin at home. Imaging showed stable transplanted organs with no signs of rejection or complications. She was discharged on oral ciprofloxacin, continued immunosuppression, and home nursing support, with plans to follow up with her nephrologist.
